clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old unmarried woman presented with a 2-month history of abdominal lump, pain, and intermittent fever with chills. Physical examination revealed a 10x8.5 cm mass in the left lower abdomen and pallor. Laboratory evaluation showed normal tumor markers and negative serology for HIV, HBV, and HCV. CECT abdomen demonstrated a 10x9.5x9.0 cm heterogeneous enhancing solid-cystic lesion with septations in the left ovary. The patient underwent surgical resection of the mass. Histopathological examination of the resected ovarian tissue revealed dense inflammation, necrosis, and florid fungal septate hyphae with dichotomous branching diagnostic of Aspergillosis. Following diagnosis, the patient was treated with intravenous voriconazole (6 mg/kg/day) and liposomal amphotericin B (0.5 mg/kg/day) for ten days.
